errors.evidence: The accepted modern correspondence (documented in scholarly work and in the Unicode Standard, “Cuneiform Numbers and Punctuation”) is as follows: – The sign “𒐜” is conventionally used to denote “10.” – The sign “𒐐” is used to denote “1.” – The sign “𒐚” is used to denote “6.”
errors.description: The agent misinterpreted the tool output by incorrectly assigning values to the cuneiform symbols.

errors.evidence: Thinking through the problem, we must “read” the ancient numeral correctly.
errors.description: The agent misunderstood the task by focusing on the incorrect aspect of the problem.

errors.evidence: The final Arabic numeral for the given Babylonian numeral 𒐜 𒐐𒐚 is 607. This result is obtained by noting that in Babylonian numerals the left group (𒐜) represents 10 and the right group (𒐐𒐚) combines to represent 1 + 6 = 7, so the overall number in base‑60 is 10×60 + 7 = 607.
errors.description: The agent misinterpreted the tool output by incorrectly assuming the value of the left group (𒐜) as 10 instead of 1.
